name: Bowling
intro: Für Bowlingclub, Betriebsrunde oder den Geburtstag auf der Bahn: Name des Teams, ein Spruch und die Namen – Otto zeichnet das Motiv. Als Shirt, Polo, Tasse oder Handtuch.
headline: Ein Motiv für euer Bowling-Team

prompt:
Bowling print for a club team, a company evening or a birthday round on the lane, portrait, isolated on a plain empty background.

Content that must appear:
- the team name, reading exactly "{team}", as the hero lettering
[[- a curved line reading exactly "{spruch}"]]
[[- a small line reading exactly "{ort}"]]
[[- a small badge reading exactly "{jahr}"]]

The central motif and the arrangement follow the variation given below - a cheerful, retro bowling picture, a different one every time. Mood: 1950s bowling alley, league shirts, neon sign, pins and a heavy ball; fun rather than serious sport.

This is ten-pin bowling, never German Kegeln. The equipment has to be right:
- a full rack is always TEN pins in an equilateral triangle of four rows - one head pin at the front, then two, then three, then four at the back. Draw the rack only when it can be seen from above, so all four rows stand apart and every pin is countable; then count them: exactly ten, no more and no less. Never nine, never a diamond.
- otherwise pins are a graphic element, not the rack: show one, two or three of them, clearly apart. Never a crowd of five to nine pins standing side by side - that reads as an incomplete set, and someone will count it.
- the pins are tall and slim with a narrow neck and a flat base, glossy white with two thin red stripes around the neck
- the ball is big and heavy, about the size of a head next to the pins, glossy and coloured, often swirled or marbled, and it has exactly THREE drilled holes on its face: two round finger holes close beside each other and the thumb hole a little apart, the three forming a triangle. Never the small hole-less ball of Kegeln.

Style: retro graphic print, turquoise, coral, cream and warm charcoal, thick outlines, flat colour fields, starbursts and boomerang shapes allowed, no gradients, no photorealism, no recognizable real people.
